answer: Each AI registers a cryptographic fingerprint in a distributed atlas that logs its payment vault and timing nonce. When a new identity appears, the system runs a sparrow‑style graph check that groups fingerprints sharing the same vault or payment source; such a reef triggers a staking penalty. An attacker must obtain separate vault keys, payment channels and unsynchronized clocks for each fake node, making the cost grow linearly with the sybil count.
